newsitem.title: USA: Oakley falls as sunglass market hits doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Oakley falls as sunglass market hits doldrums.

text.p: Bloated inventories and a lack of dynamic new products have cast a cloud on the U.S. sunglass industry, which is suffering a slowdown in sales.
Shares of sunglass maker Oakley Inc slipped four to 11-3/8 as its largest customer, Sunglass Hut International Inc, reported November same-store sales fell 9.9 percent.

Oakley forecast fourth quarter earnings to be below the consensus estimate of $0.16 per share and sees further delays in orders from 2,022-specialty store chain Sunglass Hut, which previously requested a delay in November orders.

Sunglass Hut shares fell 5/8 to 7-5/8. Shares of Bausch & Lomb Inc, owner of Ray Ban, fell 1/4 to 36-1/8. Shares of sunglass maker Gargoyles Inc, which went public in September, fell 7/8 to 8-3/4. Its IPO was priced at $16.
"We've been expecting a weak fourth quarter due to inventory overages at Sunglass Hut," said Eli Kammerman at Salomon Brothers, who follows Bausch & Lomb's Ray Ban unit.

"People have reached a limit as to how many sunglasses they can wear," he said, noting U.S. sales of premium priced sunglasses, which sell at over $30 a pair, have declined about three to four percent in the past six months.
Analysts expect the market to remain sluggish into 1997.

"Sales trends remain soft and there will probably be some downward pressure on earnings estimates for both retailers and vendors that is likely to continue into the first half of next year," said David Buchsbaum, analyst with Southeast Research.
He said pared down inventories and some new products should begin to help the market in the second half of 1997.

Analysts said Sunglass Hut indicated it will try to get inventories down to around $145 million at the end of the year. In addition to 2,022 sunglass specialty locations, it operates 28 EyeX optical stores and 41 Watch Station stores.

"Basically, Sunglass Hut has tried to pare down inventories and change its product mix to include more fashion lines," said Buchsbaum. "The main factor behind the weaker sales trends is the sport category, of which Oakely is the primary vendor," he said, noting about 25 percent of Sunglass Hut's sales are derived from Oakely products.
Last year, Oakley's net sales jumped 39 percent to $172.8 million from $124 million, with domestic sales up 27 percent.
In its most recently reported quarter, Oakley reported third quarter earnings of $0.22 a share on sales of $67.8 million versus $0.15 a share on sales of $47.5 million.

Sunglass Hut reported today that sales for the four weeks ended November 30, 1996 were $28.1 million, up 11.8 percent from $25.2 million in the year-ago period. But comparable store sales for the four-week fiscal period decreased 9.9 percent.

Sunglass Hut chief executive officer Jack Chadsey said, "We believe the combination of our marketing efforts, the flow of new products into our stores, and the preparedness of our sales associates will help strengthen our sales trend as we approach Christmas."
Analysts said due to the seasonal nature of the business, the second quarter is typically the strongest sales period for the sunglass industry.
